headline: Bind Google sign-in to the stable account identity and harden the auth surface
summary: Google sign-in now matches a returning account on its stable identity rather than the email alone, closing an account-takeover path, alongside several request-surface hardening fixes.

items.title: Bind returning Google sign-ins to the stable account identity
items.body: A returning Google sign-in is now matched to a stored account by its stable Google subject identifier, not the email address alone. A verified email can move between two distinct Google identities over time (a Workspace administrator reassigns a departed employee's address to a new hire, or a consumer account is deleted and the address later recreated), so a match on email with a different underlying identity is refused. A local password account can likewise no longer be signed into through Google merely because the addresses coincide. Both close an account-takeover path (email recycling and cross-provider assumption).

items.title: Rate-limit the passkey authentication-options endpoint
items.body: The unauthenticated passkey login-options endpoint — which runs a WebAuthn challenge operation and writes session state on every call — now carries the same per-minute rate limit as its verify sibling, so it can no longer be driven unbounded.

items.title: Fail loudly on a non-2xx response from Google
items.body: The Google token-exchange and userinfo requests now surface the true HTTP status on a non-2xx response instead of parsing the error or HTML body as if it were a success payload — which previously masked the real failure behind an opaque downstream error.

items.title: Constant-time key-fingerprint comparison and canonical loopback classification
items.body: The audit-archive verifier now compares signing-key fingerprints in constant time (matching the project-wide timing-safe comparison discipline), and the SSRF private-address check classifies loopback names through the vendored guard primitive rather than a bare literal, so every loopback spelling is treated consistently.
